1) the inhibition of host protein and RNA synthesis requires expression of two distinct regions of the viral genome; 2) the inhibition of cellular protein synthesis is dependent on both the duration of infection and the multiplicity; and 3) the quantity of leader plus-strand RNA in VSV infected cells does not correlate with the extent of inhibition of host macromolecule synthesis.
The inhibition of protein and mRNA synthesis in mouse L-cells infected by VSV is dependent on the expression of two regions, one large and one small.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which the viral gene products inhibit cellular macromolecular synthesis.
the mechanism of the inhibition of protein synthesis by VSV.
the mechanism of inhibition of cellular protein and RNA biosynthesis in VSV-infected mouse L cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inhibition of protein synthesis is not dependent on the accumulation of plus leader RNA.
neither the small nor the large viral gene product is responsible for the inhibition of host protein and RNA synthesis.

the inhibition of host macromolecules is dependent on expression of both the large and the small region of the VSV RNA genome, but not on the quantity of leader plus-strand RNA present in the infected cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inhibition of host cell RNA and protein synthesis in VSV-infected L cells is a multigenic process, and that the inhibition of RNA synthesis requires both viral genes.
the inhibition of protein synthesis is a function of the expression of two regions on the VSV genome and that neither of the gene products is plus-strand RNA.
the inhibition of host macromolecule synthesis is a complex process which is dependent on the presence of both viral gene products and is independent of the quantity of leader plus-strand RNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inhibition of host protein and RNA synthesis does not depend on the amount of leader RNA produced.
the inhibition of protein synthesis by VSV is not due to the accumulation of leader RNA.
the extent of the inhibition of protein synthesis is not dependent on the accumulation of plus strand leader RNA.
